note: Statements `prisma migrate diff` proposes to turn a chain-built database into schema.prisma, EXCLUDING functional gaps (which are gated at hard zero by scripts/check-migration-drift.ts). These are index renames and reshapes, foreign-key re-creation, column type normalisation, and one table the chain creates that the schema no longer declares. Closing them needs DROP statements aimed at a production database whose real state is not inspectable from CI, so they are pinned rather than fixed. This number may only go down; the checker fails if it grows AND if it shrinks without this file being updated.
measuredOn: CI (postgres 16.4) reported 345 on PR #362 after the production-state reconciliation (dropping the stray affiliate_documents.file_size column closed one more structural statement; 346 was CI's number one commit earlier) | 2026-09-07 (Phase 1): lowered 345 -> 344. The wave declares all 264 of its new columns on pre-existing models, its 41 enum labels, 24 foreign keys, 12 indexes and 14 new models, so it adds no drift of its own; and R3's `vehicle_requests.buyer_opportunity_id` foreign key CLOSED one pre-existing structural statement that schema.prisma already declared and the chain lacked. Measured locally on PostgreSQL 17.6 (server_version_num 170006, production's own patch level); the pre-change chain reproduced the recorded 345 exactly on the same setup, so the delta is the wave's, not the environment's. CI remains authoritative per ifCiDisagrees.
ifCiDisagrees: CI is authoritative. The count compares catalog objects (tables, columns, indexes, foreign keys, enums), which do not vary by postgres patch version, so the two should agree — but this baseline was measured locally and the first CI run is what confirms it. If CI reports a different number, set structuralStatements to CI's number rather than arguing with it.

deferredStatements.reason: The Phase 1 wave creates e_sign_envelopes.co_buyer_id and its foreign key, but schema.prisma deliberately does not declare them. lib/services/esign/esign-schema-gate.ts projects an explicit list of only the columns production has today, and its schema-gate test requires every ESignEnvelope scalar to be classified as present-in-production or added-by-the-two-unapplied-migrations. This column is neither. Declaring it would let an ungated read expand the full scalar list and ask for a column production does not have until this wave deploys.
deferredStatements.closesIn: Phase 8 (owns e-sign; lands the Prisma relation with the uniqueness cutover)

deferredStatements.reason: The foreign key belonging to the column above.

The expand half of the Phase 8 e-sign expand-and-contract. The column exists in the chain; the contract step and its Prisma declaration are Phase 8's. NOTE: this string cannot be anchored to its table — `prisma migrate diff` emits it as a continuation line of the multi-column `ALTER TABLE "e_sign_envelopes"` above it, so the table name is not on the same line. `expectedMatches` is what bounds it instead: a `signer_kind` column appearing on any OTHER table would make this match twice and fail the gate.
The composite unique index over signer_kind, same expand-and-contract.

deferredNote: An ENUMERATED exception, not a raised ceiling. `structuralStatements` stays at its measured value (344) and every other statement is still gated by it: a statement is excused ONLY if it contains one of the exact `contains` strings above, and each entry names why it is deferred and the phase that closes it. Any OTHER growth still fails the build. Adding an entry here is a reviewable diff, which is the property the ratchet is protecting. When Phase 8 lands, delete these entries — the checker fails if a deferred entry no longer matches anything, and fails if it matches more often than its declared `expectedMatches`, so an entry can neither rot into a standing excuse nor silently widen to cover a statement it was never written for.
